newsitem.title: FRANCE: French doctors check sect children after boy dies.
newsitem.headline: French doctors check sect children after boy dies.

text.p: A dozen doctors, aided by police, examined some 75 children on Monday in the homes of a U.S.-based sect in southwest France after a 19-month-old boy died from malnutrition and lack of medical care, police said.

Police raided two farms owned by the Tabitha's Place sect in Angous and Sus, near Pau, in the early morning after a magistrate placed two members of the sect under investigation on suspicion of failing to give their son Raphael adequate care.
"In the case of Raphael last week we discovered documents concerning the community which advocate corporal punishment," said state prosecutor Jean-Pierre Dreno.
"We figured people were being mistreated and that's why we're here today," he told reporters.
Investigators said some 100 adults and 70 children live at the farms in total isolation from the external world, refusing outside medical care and teaching their children at home.
Sect members Raphael Ginoux, 36, and his German-born wife Dagmar were remanded in custody at the weekend after their son Raphael died on Thursday from malnutrition and an untreated heart ailment.
